candidates.title: Evaluating AI’s Ideas: The Role of Individual Creativity and Expertise in Human-AI Co-Creativity
candidates.task: engineering design problem: solve, evaluate GPT-3.5 ideas, revise
candidates.evidence: Engineering (N=99) and psychology (N=212) students wrote a solution, evaluated pre-generated GPT-3.5 ideas, then revised; raters scored originality and effectiveness, and both groups improved. No no-AI control group is described.

candidates.title: ChatGPT as an inventor: eliciting the strengths and weaknesses of current large language models against humans in engineering design
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39, e6
other_versions: doi 10.1017/pds.2024.202 (Proceedings of the Design Society 4 paper on the same hackathon: 'Benchmarking AI design skills: insights from ChatGPT's participation in a prototyping hackathon')
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT-4 directed two participants who executed its instructions and competed against graduate-student teams; it finished second of six, with strong concept generation but design fixation and premature abandonment of concepts.

candidates.title: How AI Processing Delays Foster Creativity: Exploring Research Question Co-Creation with an LLM-based Agent
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '24), 1-25
other_versions: arXiv 2310.06155 ('CoQuest: Exploring Research Question Co-Creation with an LLM-based Agent')
candidates.task: research-question generation with an LLM agent
candidates.evidence: 20 HCI researchers used the CoQuest agent under breadth-first and depth-first generation designs (an AI-configuration comparison). Outcomes were participants' creativity ratings of research questions and the number generated, which rose with AI processing delays.

candidates.title: Divergent creativity in humans and large language models
candidates.task: Divergent Association Task, haiku, story synopses, flash fiction
candidates.evidence: Compares semantic divergence of several LLMs with a dataset of 100,000 humans on the DAT and three creative-writing tasks; LLMs beat the average human on the DAT but stay below the more creative half of humans. Distinct from the already-collected Wang et al. Nature Human Behaviour paper with a similar title.

candidates.title: Co-Writing with Opinionated Language Models Affects Users’ Views
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2023 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-15
candidates.evidence: Treatment writers used an LM assistant configured to argue one side of whether social media is good for society; their posts (judged by 500 raters) and later attitudes moved toward the model's stance. The outcome is opinion convergence toward the AI, not creativity.

candidates.title: DesignAID: Using Generative AI and Semantic Diversity for Design Inspiration
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the ACM Collective Intelligence Conference (CI '23), 1-11
candidates.evidence: 87 crowd designers compared LLM-to-image idea generation with a Pinterest image-search baseline at high or low idea diversity. Outcomes were designers' ratings of inspiration, enjoyment and usefulness, not rated output creativity.

candidates.title: Your Brain on ChatGPT: Accumulation of Cognitive Debt when Using an AI Assistant for Essay Writing Task
candidates.evidence: 54 participants wrote essays in three sessions as LLM, search-engine or brain-only groups; in a fourth session 18 switched (LLM-to-brain, brain-to-LLM). Teachers and an AI judge scored essays, and NLP found within-group homogeneity of named entities, n-grams and topics.

candidates.title: Understanding ChatGPT’s impact on student-team ideation outcomes for new product development
candidates.task: team ideation for new product development
candidates.evidence: Undergraduates ideated in two workshops, one ChatGPT-assisted (n=22) and one with analogue methods only (n=17). The analogue group produced over twice as many ideas and slightly higher flexibility and originality.

candidates.title: The Unlikely Duel: Evaluating Creative Writing in LLMs through a Unique Scenario
other_versions: Findings of EMNLP 2023 paper 'A Confederacy of Models: a Comprehensive Evaluation of LLMs on Creative Writing' (already collected)
candidates.task: humorous creative writing from one fixed prompt
candidates.evidence: Short summary version of the already-collected 'A Confederacy of Models': LLMs and human writers answered the same prompt and raters scored fluency, style, originality and humor; humans kept a lead in originality.

candidates.title: Art or Artifice? Large Language Models and the False Promise of Creativity
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '24), 1-34
candidates.task: short stories by professional authors vs LLMs (TTCW)
candidates.evidence: Ten creative writers applied 14 binary Torrance-inspired tests to 48 stories written by professional authors or LLMs. LLM stories passed 3 to 10 times fewer tests.

candidates.title: Can artificial intelligence support creativity in early design processes?
candidates.evidence: 40 design students were randomly assigned to two groups; in phase 1 one group used a text-to-image tool and the other did not, and in phase 2 both designed without AI. Professionals rated outcomes on the Creative Product Semantic Scale; cognitive load was also measured.

candidates.title: The Ideation-Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas
candidates.evidence: 43 expert researchers were randomly assigned to execute research ideas written by experts or generated by an LLM; blind reviews after execution show LLM ideas lost more on novelty, excitement and effectiveness, closing or reversing the ideation-stage gap.

candidates.title: Probing the “Creativity” of Large Language Models: Can models produce divergent semantic association?
candidates.venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2023, 12881-12888
candidates.evidence: Administers the DAT to several LLMs under different decoding strategies and compares scores with human norms; GPT-4 with greedy search exceeds 96% of humans.

candidates.title: The originality of machines: AI takes the Torrance Test
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT (GPT-4) took the TTCT and was compared with human samples and national percentiles; it scored in the top 1% for originality and fluency (abstract read from a DOAJ search snippet).

candidates.title: Is artificial intelligence more creative than humans?
other_versions: doi 10.31234/osf.io/jzt72 (PsyArXiv preprint 'Is AI More Creative Than Humans? ChatGPT and the Divergent Association Task')
candidates.evidence: GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 completed the DAT and were compared with a large human baseline; both exceeded human means, and the author questions whether this shows creativity.

candidates.title: CreativeConnect: Supporting Reference Recombination for Graphic Design Ideation with Generative AI
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '24), 1-25
candidates.task: graphic design ideation from reference images
candidates.evidence: A user study (N=16) compared CreativeConnect with a baseline system without generative pipelines; users produced more design ideas with higher self-reported creativity.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence Enhances Human Creativity Through Real-Time Evaluative Feedback
candidates.authors: de Chantal, Beaty, Laverghetta et al.
candidates.task: solutions to real-world problems and visual sketches
candidates.evidence: A preregistered online experiment (N=554) and a year-long museum field experiment (N=36,198) gave real-time originality feedback from trained AI scoring models, which raised originality in verbal and visual tasks. The AI evaluates ideas rather than generating them.

candidates.title: How funny is ChatGPT? A comparison of human- and A.I.-produced jokes
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT 3.5 and laypeople answered the same humor prompts, and ChatGPT headlines were compared with The Onion; blind raters judged the AI output equally funny or funnier.

candidates.title: Does human–AI collaboration lead to more creative art? Aesthetic evaluation of human-made and AI-generated haiku poetry
candidates.evidence: 385 participants rated haiku by professional poets, AI haiku with no human intervention, and AI haiku selected by humans (human in the loop); human-in-the-loop haiku received the highest ratings (abstract from a search snippet).

candidates.title: The Differential Role of Human Capital in Generative AI’s Impact on Creative Tasks
other_versions: arXiv 2412.03963 ('Augmenting Minds or Automating Skills: The Differential Role of Human Capital in Generative AI's Impact on Creative Tasks')
candidates.task: flash fiction writing and song composition
candidates.evidence: Two randomized controlled experiments in flash fiction writing and song composition; AI help raised outcomes more for people with higher general human capital and reduced the value of domain expertise.

candidates.title: Stylometric comparisons of human versus AI-generated creative writing
candidates.task: short stories from fixed narrative prompts
candidates.evidence: Burrows' Delta and clustering show human stories form broad, heterogeneous clusters, while GPT-3.5, GPT-4 and Llama outputs are stylistically uniform and cluster tightly by model.

candidates.title: Supermind Ideator: How Scaffolding Human-AI Collaboration Can Increase Creativity
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the ACM Collective Intelligence Conference (CI '24), 18-28
other_versions: arXiv 2311.01937 (earlier system description: 'Supermind Ideator: Exploring generative AI to support creative problem-solving')
candidates.evidence: In an experiment, people using the scaffolded LLM tool generated significantly more innovative ideas than people using plain ChatGPT or working alone (an AI vs no-AI and AI-configuration comparison).

candidates.title: Artificial Hivemind: The Open-Ended Homogeneity of Language Models (and Beyond)
candidates.venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems 38 (NeurIPS 2025), 90705-90774
candidates.evidence: Model-level study: open-ended generation shows strong repetition within models and homogeneity across models. It has 31,250 human preference annotations but no human-produced outputs; included as homogenization context.

candidates.title: Poor Alignment and Steerability of Large Language Models: Evidence from College Admission Essays
other_versions: Workshop version 'Poor alignment and steerability of large language models: Evidence using 30,000 college admissions essays' (First Workshop on Social Simulation with LLMs, per citing references)
candidates.evidence: Compares lexical and sentence variation in essays by 30,000 applicants with LLM essays from the same prompts, with and without demographic prompting. Synthetic essays were more similar to each other than to human essays, so prompting did not relieve homogenization.

candidates.title: No Longer Trending on Artstation: Prompt Analysis of Generative AI Art
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence in Music, Sound, Art and Design (EvoMUSART 2024), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, 279-295
candidates.evidence: Analysis of over 3 million prompts and generated images shows prompting focuses on surface aesthetics and popular conventional imagery, reinforcing cultural norms.

candidates.title: How Problematic Writer-AI Interactions (Rather than Problematic AI) Hinder Writers' Idea Generation
candidates.task: student writing with auto-complete or Socratic AI assistants
candidates.evidence: Case study of students writing with auto-complete or Socratic AI assistants; the number of new ideas depended on how writers interacted with the AI more than on the assistant type. No controlled creativity scoring is described.

candidates.title: The cognitive impact of ChatGPT in higher education: A systematic review of critical and creative thinking outcomes
candidates.task: higher education, critical and creative thinking
candidates.evidence: PRISMA systematic review of 67 empirical studies (2022-2025) on ChatGPT and university students' critical and creative thinking; effects depend on scaffolded versus unstructured use (abstract from a search snippet).

candidates.title: Understanding Design Fixation in Generative Artificial Intelligence
candidates.authors: Song, Zheng, Jing, Hansen, Sun, Chen
candidates.venue: ASME IDETC-CIE 2025, Volume 4 (DEC, DFMLC, DTM), V004T06A003
other_versions: arXiv 2502.05870 ('Understanding Design Fixation in Generative AI')
candidates.task: design ideation with text and image generators
candidates.evidence: Ten designers examined design fixation in outputs of text- and image-generation models at the level of design features and how they recognized and responded to it. The study concerns limited novelty and diversity of GenAI output, not an AI vs no-AI comparison.

candidates.title: Conceptual Design Generation Using Large Language Models
candidates.venue: ASME IDETC-CIE 2023, Volume 6: 35th International Conference on Design Theory and Methodology (DTM), V006T06A021
candidates.task: conceptual design solutions for 12 design problems
candidates.evidence: LLM solutions to 12 design problems were compared with crowdsourced solutions using expert ratings and computational metrics; LLM solutions scored higher on feasibility and usefulness, crowdsourced ones on novelty.

candidates.title: Pron vs Prompt: Can Large Language Models already Challenge a World-Class Fiction Author at Creative Text Writing?
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, 19654-19670
candidates.task: short stories from titles (novelist vs GPT-4)
candidates.evidence: Novelist Patricio Pron and GPT-4 each proposed 30 titles and wrote stories for all of them; literary experts rated the texts with a Boden-inspired rubric and found GPT-4 far behind, though more creative with the novelist's titles.

candidates.title: Small Language Models can Outperform Humans in Short Creative Writing: A Study Comparing SLMs with Humans and LLMs
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Computational Linguistics (COLING 2025), 6552-6570
candidates.evidence: 68 participants rated stories by human writers and a fine-tuned BART-large model; the model scored above average humans overall, with no significant human advantage on creativity, and GPT-4o used more predictable language.

candidates.title: Is Chatgpt a menace for creative writing ability? An experiment
candidates.evidence: 600 students from 10 universities were divided into a control group and an experimental group that used ChatGPT while writing; machine and human assessments of originality, content presentation, accuracy and elaboration showed a detrimental association.

candidates.title: Experimental narratives: A comparison of human crowdsourced storytelling and AI storytelling
candidates.task: short stories from identical Pygmalion-style prompts
candidates.evidence: Compares 250 crowdworker stories (2019) with 80 GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 stories from the same prompts; AI narratives were more progressive on gender roles but less imaginative in scenarios and rhetoric.

candidates.title: Case study: is there a space for TRIZ in the era of ChatGPT?
candidates.evidence: Industrial case study comparing team-generated solutions with solutions from LLMs and TRIZ-enhanced LLMs; precedes the already-collected Čok et al. (2026) TRIZ experiment.

candidates.title: AI-Augmented Brainwriting: Investigating the use of LLMs in group ideation
candidates.authors: Shaer, Cooper, Mokryn, Kun, Ben Shoshan
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '24), 1-17
candidates.evidence: Groups used an LLM-augmented brainwriting process; the authors evaluated the ideation process and resulting solution space and compared an LLM idea-evaluation engine with three expert and six novice raters.

candidates.title: Human-like problem-solving abilities in large language models using ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT solved 30 verbal insight problems, and its solution rates were compared with human rates (20 subjects) reported in a prior study.

candidates.title: The Effects of Generative AI Platforms on Undergraduates’ Narrative Intelligence and Writing Self-Efficacy
candidates.evidence: Pretest-posttest comparison of 64 undergraduates using conventional story platforms or generative AI platforms (Sudowrite, Jasper, Shortly AI); the AI group gained more in narrative intelligence and writing self-efficacy, with no difference in creative identity.

candidates.title: Diminished diversity-of-thought in a standard large language model
candidates.evidence: GPT-3.5 replications of Many Labs 2 studies gave near-zero variation on many questions (a 'correct answer' effect), far less response diversity than the human samples.

candidates.title: The Dynamics of Collective Creativity in Human-AI Hybrid Societies
candidates.task: iterative story creation in 5x5 social networks
candidates.evidence: Humans and AI agents in human-only, AI-only and hybrid networks selected, modified and shared stories over many iterations; AI-only networks were first more creative and diverse (human ratings), but hybrid networks later became more diverse than AI-only ones.

candidates.title: One fish, two fish, but not the whole sea: Alignment reduces language models’ conceptual diversity
candidates.task: conceptual judgments in two domains with human data
candidates.evidence: Compares the conceptual diversity of simulated LLM populations with human behavioral data; no model reaches human-like diversity, and aligned models are less diverse than instruction-tuned ones.

candidates.title: A large-scale comparison of human-written versus ChatGPT-generated essays
candidates.evidence: Teachers rated human-written and ChatGPT-generated argumentative essays; ChatGPT essays received higher quality ratings and showed different linguistic features. The outcome is essay quality and style, not creativity (borderline).

candidates.title: “Who” Is the Best Creative Thinking Partner? An Experimental Investigation of Human–Human, Human–Internet, and Human–AI Co‐Creation
candidates.venue: The Journal of Creative Behavior 59(3), e1519
candidates.task: alternate uses, consequences and problem-solving tasks
candidates.evidence: Between-group experiment (N=202): human-human dyads, human-Internet, and two human-ChatGPT groups (basic or specific instructions). Human dyads scored higher on divergent thinking; problem solving did not differ.

candidates.title: AIdeation: Designing a Human-AI Collaborative Ideation System for Concept Designers
candidates.authors: Wang, Lu, Ponsa i Campanyà, Chen, Chen
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-28
candidates.evidence: A user study with 16 professional designers compared AIdeation with their current tools and workflows; it raised creativity, ideation efficiency and satisfaction (all p<.01), followed by a one-week field study in four studios.

candidates.title: Human-AI Co-Creation in Product Ideation: the Dual View of Quality and Diversity
candidates.evidence: Two online experiments compare ideas from humans, GPT-4 and several co-creation modes on quality and diversity (human and deep-learning evaluations). Human ideas are diverse but lower in quality, GPT ideas the reverse, and human ideas revised with GPT balance the two.

candidates.title: Echoes in AI: Quantifying lack of plot diversity in LLM outputs
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 122(35), e2504966122
candidates.evidence: The Sui Generis score shows GPT-4 and LLaMA-3 stories repeat plot elements across generations and across models, while plots of the original human-written stories are rarely echoed.

candidates.title: Divergent LLM Adoption and Heterogeneous Convergence Paths in Research Writing
candidates.evidence: Detects ChatGPT-revised style in over 627,000 arXiv papers; difference-in-differences shows LLM use drives convergence in academic writing, strongest for early adopters, male, non-native and junior researchers.

candidates.title: Designing Interactions with Generative AI for Art and Creativity: A Systematic Review and Taxonomy
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 ACM Designing Interactive Systems Conference (DIS '25), 1126-1155
candidates.task: interactive GenAI systems for art and creativity
candidates.evidence: Systematic review of 189 interactive GenAI systems for art and creativity in HCI with a taxonomy of interaction designs; it maps system designs, not effects on creativity (low relevance).

candidates.title: AI as Humanity's Salieri: Quantifying Linguistic Creativity of Language Models via Systematic Attribution of Machine Text against Web Text
candidates.task: linguistic creativity of texts vs web text (Creativity Index)
candidates.evidence: The Creativity Index measures how much of a text can be rebuilt from web snippets; professional human authors score on average 66.2% higher than LLMs, and alignment lowers LLM scores by 30.1%.

candidates.title: The Homogenizing Engine: AI's Role in Standardizing Culture and the Path to Policy
candidates.venue: Policy Insights from the Behavioral and Brain Sciences 13(1), 14-27
candidates.evidence: Narrative policy review drawing on recent empirical studies of how LLMs reduce cultural diversity in representation, communication style and knowledge, with proposed interventions; no new data.

candidates.title: Amuse: Human-AI Collaborative Songwriting with Multimodal Inspirations
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-28
candidates.task: songwriting with chord suggestions from multimodal inputs
candidates.evidence: A user study with songwriters found the multimodal-LLM chord assistant helped turn image, text or audio ideas into musical suggestions and enhanced agency and creativity; the comparison condition and scoring are not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: PersonaFlow: Designing LLM-Simulated Expert Perspectives for Enhanced Research Ideation
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 ACM Designing Interactive Systems Conference (DIS '25)
candidates.evidence: User studies found that LLM-simulated expert personas raised the perceived relevance and creativity of research directions and critical-thinking activity without raising cognitive load.

candidates.title: MacGyver: Are Large Language Models Creative Problem Solvers?
candidates.evidence: Over 1,600 problems needing unconventional object use were given to LLMs and humans; humans did well on familiar tasks with higher variance, while LLMs attempted more problems but proposed physically infeasible actions.

candidates.title: Are Large Language Models Capable of Generating Human-Level Narratives?
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2024 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing, 17659-17681
candidates.evidence: Discourse-level analysis with expert and automatic annotations finds human stories suspenseful and diverse in structure, while LLM stories are homogeneously positive and lack tension.

candidates.title: Effects of ChatGPT use on undergraduate students’ creativity: a threat to creative thinking?
candidates.task: 10 weeks of ChatGPT-supported assignments; CREA creativity test
candidates.evidence: One-group pretest-posttest design: 31 undergraduates used ChatGPT for course assignments for 10 weeks, and creativity measured with the CREA test showed no evidence of decline (53.57% improved, 25% declined).

candidates.title: Expertise Elevates AI Usage: Experimental Evidence Comparing Laypeople and Professional Artists
candidates.authors: Eisenmann, Karjus, Canet Sola, Brinkmann, Supriyatno, Rahwan
candidates.task: image replication and creative image creation with a text-to-image tool
candidates.evidence: Preregistered comparison of 50 professional artists and matched laypeople using a text-to-image AI; artists made more accurate copies and more divergent ideas, and GPT-4o was also benchmarked. Everyone used AI, so there is no no-AI arm; journal version published 2026-05-18.

candidates.title: AI Writing Assistants Influence Topic Choice in Self-Presentation
candidates.venue: Extended Abstracts of the 2023 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-6
candidates.evidence: 200 participants wrote self-introductions with an assistant fine-tuned to favor interest, work or hospitality topics; the model's topic preference shifted the topics people wrote about (content convergence toward the AI).

candidates.title: Can Good Writing Be Generative? Expert-Level AI Writing Emerges through Fine-Tuning on High Quality Books
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-27
candidates.task: emulating the styles of 50 acclaimed authors
candidates.evidence: 28 MFA writers competed with three LLMs; 28 expert and 131 lay judges made blind pairwise comparisons. Experts preferred human writing in 82.7% of cases with in-context prompting, but preferred AI in 62% after fine-tuning on authors' works.

candidates.title: The widespread adoption of large language model-assisted writing across society
candidates.authors: Liang, Zhang, Codreanu, Wang, Cao, Zou
candidates.task: consumer complaints, press releases, job postings, UN press releases
candidates.evidence: Estimates LLM-assisted writing across four corpora (2022-2024), about 18% of financial consumer complaints and 24% of corporate press releases by late 2024. Prevalence only; no diversity or creativity outcome.

candidates.title: Quantifying large language model usage in scientific papers
other_versions: arXiv 2404.01268 ('Mapping the Increasing Use of LLMs in Scientific Papers')
candidates.evidence: Large-scale analysis of 950,965 papers estimating the share of LLM-modified text over time and across fields (from the arXiv abstract). Prevalence only; no diversity outcome; companion to the already-collected peer-review study.

candidates.title: Delving into LLM-assisted writing in biomedical publications through excess vocabulary
other_versions: arXiv 2406.07016 ('Delving into ChatGPT usage in academic writing through excess vocabulary', already collected)
candidates.evidence: Published version of the already-collected arXiv paper: excess-word analysis of over 15 million biomedical abstracts shows an abrupt rise in LLM style words, implying at least 13.5% of 2024 abstracts were LLM-processed.

candidates.title: Is ChatGPT Transforming Academics' Writing Style?
candidates.evidence: Word-frequency analysis of one million arXiv abstracts estimates a rising share of ChatGPT-style abstracts, about 35% in computer science. Style prevalence; no diversity measure.

candidates.title: Delving into PubMed records: some terms in medical writing have drastically changed after the arrival of ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: Tracks 142 potentially AI-influenced terms against 84 control terms in PubMed; 100 rose sharply in 2024, suggesting ChatGPT accelerated vocabulary shifts. No diversity measure.

candidates.title: Do LLMs write like humans? Variation in grammatical and rhetorical styles
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 122(8), e2422455122
candidates.task: parallel human and LLM text corpora
candidates.evidence: Biber's lexical, grammatical and rhetorical features show systematic differences between human and LLM texts (Llama 3, GPT-4o); LLMs fail to match human stylistic variation, more so when instruction-tuned.

candidates.title: Generative artificial intelligence in creative contexts: a systematic review and future research agenda
candidates.evidence: Systematic literature review of 64 studies on GenAI in creative contexts covering methods, trends, and implications for creative outcomes and industry practice.

candidates.title: How does generative artificial intelligence impact student creativity?
candidates.task: Alternate Uses Task in a college creativity course
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods study in a college creativity course scored fluency, flexibility, elaboration and originality on the AUT to assess how ChatGPT-3 affects students' divergent thinking (abstract from a DOAJ search snippet).

candidates.title: Comparing the Ideation Quality of Humans With Generative Artificial Intelligence
candidates.evidence: Blind expert evaluation of ideas from human professionals and an AI system; AI ideas scored higher on novelty and customer benefit with similar feasibility and made up most of the top ideas.

candidates.title: Humans create more novelty than ChatGPT when asked to retell a story
candidates.authors: Breithaupt, Otenen, Wright, Kruschke, Li, Tan
candidates.evidence: Compares chains of three retellings by different people with chains by ChatGPT accounts; humans add 55-60% novel words and concepts per retelling, while ChatGPT changes little after its first summary.

candidates.title: Large language models, social demography, and hegemony: comparing authorship in human and synthetic text
candidates.authors: Alvero, Lee, Regla-Vargas, Kizilcec, Joachims, Antonio
candidates.evidence: Compares writing-style features of over 150,000 admissions essays with over 25,000 GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 essays to the same prompts; human essays vary more, and AI essays most resemble those of male, more privileged applicants.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligence in communication impacts language and social relationships
candidates.evidence: Two randomized experiments with smart-reply suggestions: AI replies raised communication speed and positive emotional language and changed partner perceptions. The outcome is language tone, not creativity or diversity; context on AI shaping expression (cited by Sourati et al. 2026).

candidates.title: Exploring the impact of AI features on collaborative creativity
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 36th Australasian Conference on Human-Computer Interaction (OzCHI '24), 480-489
candidates.task: pair ideation in a digital collaboration tool
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment with 36 participants in pairs, with or without AI features for divergent thinking, sense-making and convergent thinking; AI pairs produced more novel but less appropriate ideas (not statistically significant).

candidates.title: GenAI Creativity in Narrative Tasks: Exploring New Forms of Creativity
candidates.evidence: Benchmarks ChatGPT against human performance on standardized creativity tests; ChatGPT showed high fluency but average creative output.

candidates.title: The paradox of creativity in generative AI: high performance, human-like bias, and limited differential evaluation
candidates.task: egg task (fixation and original idea generation)
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT-4o did the egg task and was compared with 47 human participants and data from eight earlier studies; it was more productive but showed a similar fixation bias and weak evaluation of originality.

candidates.title: The effects of generative AI model type and visual stimuli type on design creativity
candidates.venue: Artificial Intelligence for Engineering Design, Analysis and Manufacturing 39, e17
candidates.task: early-stage design ideation in design education
candidates.evidence: Controlled experiment varying generative AI tool type and visual stimulus type; text-to-image tools and abstract visuals raised design creativity in divergent and convergent thinking, with a warning about fixation.

candidates.title: Exploring the use of generative text AI in design creativity inquiries
candidates.venue: Computers in Human Behavior: Artificial Humans 6, 100219
candidates.task: creative design course inquiries with text GenAI
candidates.evidence: Non-design students used text-based GenAI in structured design-creativity inquiries, and peers rated the ideas on originality, practicality, surprise and relevance. No comparison condition is described (abstract from a search snippet).

candidates.title: The power of generative marketing: Can generative AI create superhuman visual marketing content?
candidates.venue: International Journal of Research in Marketing 42(1), 13-31
candidates.evidence: Three studies compare AI-generated and human-made marketing images on perceived quality, creativity and field ad performance (over 250,000 ratings, 173,000 impressions); AI images matched or beat human images. Partly a perception study (abstract from search snippets).

candidates.title: The Double-Edged Roles of Generative AI in the Creative Process: Experiments on Design Work
candidates.task: design work, ideation and execution stages
candidates.evidence: Controlled lab experiments with students and field tests with professional designers: GenAI raised creativity in ideation for all users, but in execution it helped novices while experts spent more time without creativity gains.

candidates.title: Exploring creativity in human–AI co-creation: a comparative study across design experience
candidates.task: design process, novice and experienced designers
candidates.evidence: Comparative experiment of a human-AI co-creative design process versus a traditional process; the AI process raised creative performance, mainly idea generation for novices and refinement for experienced designers.

candidates.title: Human-generative AI collaboration enhances task performance but undermines human’s intrinsic motivation
candidates.task: professional tasks in four online experiments
candidates.evidence: Four online experiments (N=3,562): working with GenAI raised immediate task performance, but the gain did not carry over to later solo tasks and intrinsic motivation fell. Whether outcomes include creativity ratings is not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Beyond Cognitive Support: Social Interaction and Affective Experience in AI-Assisted Creative Thinking Among University Students
candidates.evidence: 92 undergraduates solved creative problems with GPT-4; structural equation models link perceived social interaction and positive affect during collaboration to convergent (not divergent) thinking scores. All used AI; correlational design.

candidates.title: Artificial intelligence and its impact on creativity and diversity: An empirical study of large language model-generated product ideas
candidates.authors: Terwiesch, Meincke, Girotra, Mollick, Nave, Ulrich
other_versions: arXiv 2607.27553 ('AI and Its Impact on Creativity and Diversity: An Empirical Study of LLM-Generated Product Ideas', posted 2026-07-30)
Related already-collected working papers: Girotra et al. (2023) 'Ideas Are Dimes a Dozen' and Meincke, Mollick and Terwiesch (2024) 'Prompting Diverse Ideas'
candidates.task: new product ideas for college students under $50
candidates.evidence: A series of studies: LLM product ideas have higher average purchase intent and are 7 times more likely to rank in the top 10%, but are less novel and less diverse; newer models, pooling and prompting narrow the diversity gap. Appears to publish the already-collected Girotra et al. and Meincke et al. studies.

candidates.title: Effects of AI viewpoint divergence on group creative performance: Cognitive-neural mechanisms
candidates.task: dyad-AI collaboration on scientific and everyday creativity tasks
candidates.evidence: 89 dyads were randomly assigned to work with an AI giving high- or low-divergence viewpoints; high divergence raised idea novelty only in everyday tasks and lowered usefulness in both, with fNIRS hyperscanning of prefrontal activity.

candidates.title: Generative AI Makes Creative Output More Homogeneous
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 European Conference on Cognitive Ergonomics (ECCE 2026), 198-201
other_versions: Already-collected full review: de Rooij and Biskjaer (2026), 'Does generative AI make us think alike? A systematic review and meta-analysis of homogenisation effects in human-AI co-creation'
candidates.task: meta-analysis of homogenization in human-AI co-creation
candidates.evidence: Systematic review and meta-analysis of 19 studies (61 effect sizes) finds a small, significant homogenization effect of AI use (d = .334). Short conference version of the already-collected de Rooij and Biskjaer (2026) meta-analysis.

candidates.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and Design Co-Creation in Luxury New Product Development: The Power of Discarded Ideas
candidates.task: luxury t-shirt design (human-only vs AI-recommended designs)
candidates.evidence: T-shirts were designed by human designers alone or from AI design recommendations interpreted by designers; in a controlled experiment with over 1,000 consumers the AI-based designs were preferred when the source was hidden, and 20-week sales rose. Outcome is consumer preference and sales, not rated creativity.

candidates.title: Generative Artificial Intelligence and the Creative Industries: A Bibliometric Review and Research Agenda
candidates.task: bibliometric mapping of GenAI in creative industries
candidates.evidence: PRISMA-based bibliometric review of 119 articles (2023-2025) mapping thematic clusters; notes a gap in comparative empirical studies. Not an effect synthesis (low relevance).

candidates.title: Evaluating Creativity Support Tools via Homogenization Analysis
candidates.venue: Extended Abstracts of the CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI EA '24), 1-7
other_versions: Companion to the already-collected Anderson, Shah and Kreminski (2024) Creativity & Cognition paper
candidates.evidence: Proposes the homogenization of users' outputs (embedding similarity) as a general evaluation criterion for creativity support tools and demonstrates the analysis.

candidates.title: Supporting Brainstorming with a Collaborative Platform or a Generative Artificial Intelligence Tool: An Exploratory Study
candidates.authors: Gerardini, Sarcinella, Borghesi, Pozzi, Gaggioli, Chirico
candidates.task: group brainstorming with Miro or DALL-E, online or offline
candidates.evidence: Sixteen groups of five used Miro or DALL-E online or offline in a 2x2 design; two raters scored fluency, elaboration, flexibility and originality, and online DALL-E sessions produced more elaborated ideas.

candidates.title: Unlocking creativity with artificial intelligence (AI): Field and experimental evidence on the Goldilocks (curvilinear) effect of human–AI collaboration
candidates.evidence: Two experiments assigned 139 business professionals and 319 working adults to collaborate with ChatGPT to different degrees; moderate collaboration gave the highest creativity (human judges, entrepreneurs, AI scoring) via more diverse ideas. A survey of 188 creative workers replicated the pattern.

candidates.title: The effects of generative AI on collaborative problem-solving and team creativity performance in digital story creation: an experimental study
candidates.venue: International Journal of Educational Technology in Higher Education 22, 23
candidates.evidence: Sixty university students were randomly assigned to create digital stories with GAI tools (ChatGPT, Midjourney, Runway) or with traditional methods; the GAI group scored higher on team creativity (novelty, user experience) and collaborative problem solving.

candidates.title: Symbiosis or stagnation? Investigating the impact of AI on creativity in L1 Chinese writing
candidates.evidence: Abstract not retrievable (publisher blocks scripts; none in Crossref or Semantic Scholar). The title indicates an empirical study of AI's effect on creativity in L1 Chinese writing; design unconfirmed. Cited by Ahsan et al. (2026).

candidates.title: Augmentation or limitation? Generative AI’s influence on college students’ creative problem-solving
candidates.evidence: Abstract not retrievable; the title indicates an empirical study of how generative AI affects college students' creative problem solving. Design unconfirmed; cited by Ahsan et al. (2026).

candidates.title: The Double-Edged Sword of Creative Control in Designer-AI Co-Creation with Design Experience as a Boundary Condition
candidates.evidence: Scenario-based between-subjects experiment with 226 designers and design students varying creative control over the AI; control raised design creativity through ownership and lowered it through cognitive load, moderated by experience. The creativity measure may be scenario-based.

candidates.title: Nonlinear Interaction with LLMs: Enhancing Divergent and Convergent Processes in Complex Information Tasks
candidates.task: complex information tasks with a nonlinear LLM interface
candidates.evidence: Abstract not retrieved; the title indicates a study of a nonlinear LLM interaction design meant to support divergent and convergent processes. Design unconfirmed; cited by de Rooij and Biskjaer (2026).

candidates.title: Harnessing generative AI for collaborative creativity: A study of university students’ engagement and innovation
candidates.venue: International Journal of Innovative Research and Scientific Studies 8(3), 3284-3296
candidates.evidence: Fifty undergraduates were divided into AI-supported and non-AI teams for the AUT; AI teams scored higher on fluency, flexibility, originality and elaboration, and students reported fixation on AI ideas.

candidates.title: Echoes of Automation: The Increasing Use of LLMs in Newsmaking
candidates.venue: Social, Cultural, and Behavioral Modeling (SBP-BRiMS 2025), Lecture Notes in Computer Science, 3-13
candidates.task: 40,000+ major, local and college news articles
candidates.evidence: AI-text detectors on over 40,000 news articles show rising GenAI use, especially in local and college news; linguistic analysis finds GenAI raises word richness, lowers formality and makes writing styles more uniform.

candidates.title: Testing English News Articles for Lexical Homogenization Due to Widespread Use of Large Language Models
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 63rd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 4: Student Research Workshop), 1239-1245
candidates.evidence: Compares lexical features of English online news from 2018 and 2024; finds signs of LLM influence but no measurable homogenization (from a search snippet). Found while resolving a reference, not in a reference list.

candidates.title: Human-AI Interaction in Creative Tasks: an Experimental Investigation
candidates.task: open-ended creative writing task in the lab
candidates.evidence: Lab participants were randomly assigned to LLM access or none; independent Prolific raters scored creativity. AI access raised performance only among active users, with a concave relation to the number of queries. Found via a Crossref search while resolving a reference.

candidates.title: Future AI Systems: Human–AI Collaborative Teams Outperform Human-Only Teams in Design Ideation
candidates.evidence: Human-subject study comparing human-human teams with human-AI teams in which an AI 'Disruptive Interjector' offers suggestions; trained judges rated human-AI team ideas higher. The abstract does not say whether the AI is generative; found via a Crossref search.

candidates.title: Examining linguistic shifts in academic writing before and after the launch of ChatGPT: a study on preprint papers
candidates.evidence: After ChatGPT, arXiv abstracts show more LLM-preferred words, higher lexical complexity and sentiment, and lower syntactic complexity, cohesion and readability. A linguistic-shift study rather than a diversity measure.

candidates.title: Contrasting Linguistic Patterns in Human and LLM-Generated News Text
candidates.task: English news text vs six LLMs
candidates.evidence: Human news texts show more scattered sentence lengths and more varied vocabulary than outputs of six LLMs, and differences between LLMs and humans exceed those among LLMs.

candidates.title: AI-generated poetry is indistinguishable from human-written poetry and is rated more favorably
candidates.evidence: Per the title (abstract not retrieved), readers could not tell AI poems from human poems and rated AI poems more favorably. Mainly a perception study; included only for the AI-vs-human quality comparison.

candidates.title: Generative AI has not (yet?) surpassed humans in creative idea generation: A meta-analysis (2022-2025)
other_versions: Already-collected preprint: de Rooij and Biskjaer (2025), 'Has AI Surpassed Humans in Creative Idea Generation? A Meta-Analysis' (doi 10.31234/osf.io/9u2ke_v1)
candidates.task: meta-analysis of AI vs human idea generation
candidates.evidence: Conference abstract: meta-analysis of 17 experiments (115 effect sizes, 2022-2025) finds a small, non-significant pooled advantage for GenAI over humans. Later version of the already-collected preprint.

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence, Scientific Discovery, and Product Innovation
candidates.task: materials discovery in a corporate R&D lab
candidates.evidence: WITHDRAWN: arXiv removed it (v2, 20 May 2025) over concerns about data validity and incomplete IRB requirements. It claimed a randomized rollout of an AI materials-discovery tool to 1,018 scientists that raised discoveries and compound novelty; listed so screeners can exclude it knowingly (cited by Dell'Acqua et al.).

candidates.title: From Words to Wonder: Designing and Evaluating an AI-Empowered Creative Storytelling System for Elementary Children
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-15
candidates.evidence: Mixed-methods evaluation with 40 children (grades 2-6) found the AI co-creation system StoryPrompt improved storytelling creativity and richness compared with a storyboard method.

candidates.title: CoExploreDS: Framing and Advancing Collaborative Design Space Exploration Between Human and AI
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2025 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems, 1-20
candidates.evidence: User studies found the human-AI design-space exploration system significantly improved design quality and the collaboration experience; the comparison condition is not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Wordcraft: Story Writing With Large Language Models
candidates.venue: 27th International Conference on Intelligent User Interfaces (IUI '22), 841-852
candidates.evidence: Participants wrote short stories with and without an LLM-powered editor; results describe co-writing experiences (open-ended conversation, custom rewrites, suggestions that unblock writers) rather than rated creativity.

candidates.title: Fluid Transformers and Creative Analogies: Exploring Large Language Models’ Capacity for Augmenting Cross-Domain Analogical Creativity
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 15th Conference on Creativity and Cognition (C&C '23), 489-505
candidates.task: problem reformulation with LLM cross-domain analogies
candidates.evidence: Three studies: LLM-generated cross-domain analogies were rated helpful (median 4 of 5) for problem reformulation and led to observable changes in about 80% of reformulations; up to 25% of outputs were rated potentially harmful.

candidates.title: Exploring cognitive strategies in human-AI interaction: ChatGPT's role in creative tasks
candidates.evidence: Abstract not retrievable; the title indicates an empirical study of people's cognitive strategies when using ChatGPT on creative tasks. Design and outcomes unconfirmed; cited by Zhou et al. (2026).

candidates.title: Gain or loss? The dual effects of dependence on AI on employee’s creativity
candidates.task: employees' dependence on AI and creativity
candidates.evidence: Abstract not retrievable; the title indicates a study of employees' AI dependence and their creativity, probably survey-based (the creativity measure may be self- or supervisor-rated). Included for completeness; cited by Yuan et al. (2026).

candidates.title: Stimulating design ideation with artificial intelligence: present and (short-term) future
candidates.task: AI for design inspiration and ideation
candidates.evidence: Literature review of AI support for design inspiration and ideation with a proposed framework; most reviewed contributions are demonstrations from IT. Not an effect synthesis (low relevance).

candidates.title: INFLUENCE OF IMAGE STIMULI ON DESIGN CREATIVITY: EXPLORATION OF GENERATIVE AI IN GROUP IDEATION
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the International Conference on Engineering and Product Design Education (E&PDE 2025)
candidates.task: collaborative-sketching group ideation in a design course
candidates.evidence: Each participant received an AI-generated image stimulus during group ideation; participants found the stimuli unhelpful, and evaluators judged that group collaboration, not the AI stimuli, drove the best ideas (abstract from a search snippet).

candidates.title: AI Role in Ideation for Design Creativity Enhancement
candidates.authors: Gong, Paananen, Nurmela, Gonçalves, Georgiev, Häkkilä
candidates.venue: DS 136: Proceedings of the Asia Design and Innovation Conference (ADIC) 2024
candidates.task: individual and group ideation with AI tools (students)
candidates.evidence: Seven students generated ideas individually or in groups with AI tools; the study examined AI's effect on creativity from participants' views and their outputs. Cited by Ramakrishnan (2026).

candidates.title: EXPLORING THE IMPACT OF GENERATIVE STIMULI ON THE CREATIVITY OF DESIGNERS IN COMBINATIONAL DESIGN
candidates.evidence: Twenty designers ideated with stimuli made by generative adversarial networks or with standard combinational images; generative stimuli showed advantages in the 'smoothness' of creative outcomes. GAN stimuli, not an LLM; found via search while resolving a reference.

candidates.title: ChatGPT and Me: Collaborative Creativity in a Group Brainstorming with Generative AI
candidates.evidence: Classroom study of student groups brainstorming with ChatGPT as a partner; students' prompts and ChatGPT's responses showed linguistic diversity, so ChatGPT use did not necessarily homogenize ideas (abstract from the ASEE page snippet).

candidates.title: Creative combinational design through generative AI in different dimensional representations: An exploration
candidates.authors: Wang, Han, Zhao, Yin, Chen, Childs
candidates.evidence: Two empirical studies with expert and student designers compare LLM, text-to-image and text-to-3D models on combinational design tasks; GenAI mainly helps the divergent stage by supplying more ideas (abstract from a search snippet).

candidates.title: Does ChatGPT Increase Language Homogenization?
candidates.venue: KI in Medien, Kommunikation und Marketing (Springer), 11-31
candidates.evidence: Book chapter; abstract not retrievable. The title indicates an analysis of whether ChatGPT increases language homogenization; design unconfirmed. Cited by Zastudil et al. (2025).

candidates.title: Artificial Intelligence and the creative process: Does AI-creativity extend beyond divergent thinking?
candidates.task: convergent thinking and discernment in creative problem solving
candidates.evidence: Uses creative problem-solving methods to test AI on convergent thinking and discernment beyond divergent thinking; the abstract (search snippet) does not state a human comparison.

candidates.title: AI vs humans in the AUT: Simulations to LLMs
candidates.evidence: Review of studies applying simulations and LLMs such as GPT-3 to the AUT; LLMs perform near or somewhat above human levels on originality and usefulness (abstract from a search snippet).

candidates.title: Examining the Prevalence and Dynamics of AI-Generated Media in Art Subreddits
candidates.authors: Matatov, Aubin Le Quéré, Amir, Naaman
candidates.evidence: Analyzes image posts and AI-use accusations in art subreddits through 2023; labeled AI posts were under 0.5% of image posts and newcomers used AI more. Prevalence and community dynamics only; no diversity or creativity outcome.

candidates.title: Large language models that replace human participants can harmfully misportray and flatten identity groups
candidates.evidence: Argues analytically, and shows with 4 LLMs and human studies of 3,200 participants, that LLMs prompted with identities misportray groups and flatten the diversity of their responses.

candidates.title: Towards Collaborative Brain-storming among Humans and AI Agents: An Implementation of the IBIS-based Brainstorming Support System with Multiple AI Agents
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the ACM Collective Intelligence Conference (CI '24), 1-9
candidates.task: brainstorming on a discussion platform with GPT-3.5 agents
candidates.evidence: Compared brainstorming by humans alone, humans with GPT-3.5 IBIS agents, and agents alone (two groups of three people); with agents, ideas and topics per person and per session tended to rise, with large individual variation.
